lessons.title: Professional AI Judgment and Direction
lessons.script:
Welcome back to the AI Confidence Academy. We are beginning Phase Two, Journey One, Lesson One: Professional AI Judgment and Direction.

You have learned to work with generative AI. Now we begin a different kind of practice: using those skills to produce work that is useful, can be checked, and has someone clearly responsible for the outcome.

In this lesson, we start with a familiar professional situation. A manager needs a weekly service report. AI helps organize the information into a clear summary. The writing looks finished, but one of its figures cannot be traced to the source notes.

What happens next is the heart of today's lesson.

Rather than accepting a polished answer, we will examine the source record, inspect the draft, identify the claim that needs evidence, and revise the report. You will see those steps on screen. Then you'll decide for yourself what should be kept, corrected, or withheld.

After that, we turn to a task from your work, a business you are developing, or a professional opportunity you want to explore. You will identify five capabilities you can already demonstrate, along with the evidence that supports them, and two areas where you still need to develop. Be specific. We are not making a list of tools you have tried. We are identifying abilities you can put to work and explain to another person.

Next, you will build your first human-and-AI responsibility map. You'll describe the purpose of the task, which parts an AI system may assist with, what information must be checked, and who makes the final decision. You'll use an AI assistant of your choosing to examine your notes and identify what may be missing.

The important work begins when you examine the result. Did the system add an ability you never claimed? Did it assume authority you do not have? Did it include a figure that needs an independent source? You will make a correction, explain why it matters, and keep the evidence in your Project Record.

That first record becomes part of the business project you will develop throughout Phase Two. The goal today is not to build a complicated automation. It is to establish the professional judgment that will make the workflows and systems you build worth trusting.

You'll watch the example, practice the method, and finish with a result you can explain.

At the Academy, we put it simply: AI assists. Humans verify.

Let's begin.

lessons.title: Find the Need and Establish the Evidence
lessons.script:
Welcome back to the AI Confidence Academy. We are now in Phase Two, Journey One, Lesson Two: Find the Need and Establish the Evidence. In the previous lesson, you practiced taking responsibility for the work AI helps you produce. You checked the facts before accepting a polished report. Today, we go one step earlier. Before we ask AI to build something, we ask whether we understand the actual need.

Imagine someone says, “We need a chatbot.” A chatbot might help. But why do they need it? Are customers missing information? Are employees using different instructions? Are questions reaching the wrong person? Those are different problems, and they may need different solutions.

Today, you'll learn to separate a visible symptom from its possible cause. You'll compare three needs, investigate the evidence, and use your own AI assistant to prepare fair questions rather than invent answers. By the end, you'll select one provisional need for the project you began in Lesson 1.1. Your decision will be open to correction when better evidence arrives.

You bring the purpose and judgment. AI can help you organize what you know and ask what you still need to learn. We will start with the person who needs the work to improve. Let's begin.

lessons.title: Select AI Roles and Define Business Value
lessons.script:
Welcome back to the AI Confidence Academy. We are now in Phase Two, Journey One, Lesson Three: Select AI Roles and Define Business Value. In the last lesson, you started with people and their needs. You compared possible problems, distinguished observations from assumptions, and chose one need to investigate. Today we will decide which parts of that work deserve help from AI—and which parts do not.

A business owner can save twenty minutes using AI to draft a proposal, then spend thirty minutes correcting promises the business never made. The draft was faster. The full job was not. That distinction matters whenever someone says AI saves time.

You'll match five tasks with appropriate support, compare an AI approach with a simpler non-AI alternative, and choose a measure of useful value. You will use the AI assistant you already chose, but your judgment—and your evidence—will determine the final decision.

We are not collecting AI tricks. We are developing professional ability to choose when a tool serves a real purpose. Let's begin.

lessons.title: Direct Professional Requests and Decision Support
lessons.script:
Welcome back to the AI Confidence Academy. We are now in Phase Two, Journey One, Lesson Four: Direct Professional Requests and Decision Support. You have identified a need worth investigating, examined where AI may help, and learned to measure business value rather than simply counting outputs. Today we will bring those decisions into a professional conversation with AI.

An AI assistant can produce an attractive recommendation in seconds. But if you have not supplied the purpose, the person it serves, the necessary facts, and the limitations, that recommendation may only sound convincing.

In this lesson you will learn a Professional Request Framework built around six essentials: purpose, audience, context, task, constraints and quality. Then you will ask your own AI assistant to compare two options, challenge an unsupported assumption, and decide what evidence you still need.

Your final responsibility is not to accept the recommendation. It is to make a decision you can explain and defend. We will practice with a fictional founder who has a promising business idea, but not yet enough facts to choose a service. Let's begin.
